cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Calleja's Wittgensteinian family-resemblance refusal of essentialist definition is a candidate methodological template for the dissertation's own definitional moves around 'virtual world', 'incorporation', and dimension-boundary cases. The principled rejection of necessary-and-sufficient conditions in favor of overlapping resemblances is itself a portable methodological commitment.

Calleja's distinction between game-as-object and game-as-process — where the dormant code/board pieces present a potential that is actualized during gameplay — is structurally cognate with Aristotelian potency/actuality and with phantasia-operations that animate latent images. ANTICIPATORY: Calleja does not invoke Aristotle.

Calleja's processual ontology of games (Taylor + Malaby) — games as ongoing processes that always contain potential for refiguration — invites phenomenological reading via BCAP's analyses of being-in-act vs. mere-potency. ANTICIPATORY.

Calleja's category 'virtual game environments' (the intersection of game-family and virtual-environment-family) is a candidate target for Umwelt-grounding in Layer C: every virtual game environment is a designer-constituted Umwelt with bounded perception-action affordances. ANTICIPATORY — singly anchored (Gibson-bridge falsified per Phase 0 cite-check).

The five-element descriptive framework (player / sign / coded rules / environmental properties / material medium) parallels structurally — though not by content — Burke's pentadic decomposition (Agent / Agency / Act / Scene / [implicit] Purpose). Both refuse essentialist reduction and instead distribute analytic load across irreducible ratios. ANTICIPATORY — Burke wholly absent from Calleja per Phase 0 cite-check.

phase2_special_guidance: Standard single-pass. Capture the three-axes mapping (formal / experiential / sociocultural) with care — it is foundational for the volume's self-positioning and is reused implicitly throughout Chapters 3 and 10. Note the explicit position-on-the-experiential-axis claim (p.7) and the qualification that the other two axes will inform the analysis. Capture the five-element descriptive framework as a unit (player, representational sign, coded rules, [simulated] environmental properties, material medium) — it is Calleja's load-bearing analytic decomposition before the PIM proper. Treat the Aarseth ergodic/nontrivial-sign discussion as a Tier-2 concept import (it will recur). The Suits 'lusory attitude' mention is prospective only — full treatment is Ch.3. Note that Calleja explicitly positions himself AGAINST the essentialist definition projects of Juul (2005) and Salen+Zimmerman (2003) — flag this as the volume's first explicit POSITION-edge against Tier-A interlocutors.
notes: Chapter 1 contains zero references to Aristotle, Burke, Uexkull, Merleau-Ponty, or Gibson — consistent with the Phase 0 CRITICAL FINDING. The Wittgenstein cite (Philosophical Investigations, 1997 edition) is the chapter's sole classical-philosophy anchor and is methodological rather than substantive (used solely for the family-resemblance move). Heidegger is NOT cited in this chapter (Heidegger's single appearance is in Ch.2 p.21). The chapter's role in the volume's argument is preparatory-definitional: it clears terminological space for the PIM by (a) refusing essentialism, (b) establishing virtual-game-environments as the unit of analysis, and (c) supplying the five-element framework against which the six-dimensional PIM will be elaborated. Body-form chapter title is 'Games beyond Games' (lowercase 'beyond') though manifest and TOC use title-case 'Games Beyond Games' — preserved both forms above. Subsection structure is markedly different from Chapters 4-9 (which all open with 'Macro Phase: <subtitle>'), confirming Phase 0 special_feature_flag #2.
